common.copyFailed: Could not copy. Select the text and copy it by hand.

validation.host: Enter an IP address or a host name, without a scheme, port or path
validation.portInternal: Ports {{first}} to {{last}} on 0.0.0.0 and 127.0.0.1 are kept for the node itself. Take another port or a specific address.
validation.bindIp: Enter an IPv4 address of the node, or 0.0.0.0 for all of them
validation.maskTargetInternal: The target must not be an internal port of the node ({{first}} to {{last}} on the loopback)
validation.domain: Enter a host name such as www.example.com: letters, digits, hyphens and dots, no dot at the end
validation.secret: The secret is exactly 32 hexadecimal digits (0-9, a-f)
validation.adTag: The ad tag is empty or exactly 32 hexadecimal digits
validation.limit: Enter a whole number from 0 to {{max}}
validation.hostPort: Enter host:port, such as proxy.example.com:1080, with an IPv6 address in brackets
validation.hostPortPort: The port after the last colon must be a number from 1 to 65535
validation.hostPortChars: The host cannot have spaces, control characters or any of / \ @ # ? [ ] %
validation.hostPortBrackets: Brackets are for an IPv6 address, and an IPv6 address needs them, as in [2001:db8::1]:1080
validation.passwordAgain: The address or the username is new: type the password again. A stored password is kept only for the address and the username that it was given for.
validation.usernameColon: The username of an HTTP proxy cannot have a colon (:)
validation.interface: Enter an interface name of 1 to 15 ASCII characters, without spaces, / or :
validation.sourceIp: Enter an IPv4 or IPv6 address of the node, without a port or brackets
validation.urlSpaces: A URL has no spaces or control characters
validation.checkInterval: Seconds between checks: 0 for the default of the node, or 1 to {{max}}
validation.checkTimeout: Seconds to wait for an answer: 0 for the default of the node, or 1 to {{max}}
validation.checkThreshold: Checks in a row: 0 for the default of the node, or 1 to {{max}}
validation.webDomain: A WEB proxy needs a domain of at least two labels, such as proxy.example.com
validation.basePath: Segments of letters, digits, _ and -, each starting with a letter or digit, joined by slashes, none at either end: tg or a/b
validation.basePathRequired: Behind a web server the proxy needs a base path: the path of the site that goes to it, such as tg
validation.trustedCidr: One address or prefix per line, inside the loopback or private ranges: 127.0.0.1/32, 172.17.0.0/16
validation.trustedCidrsRequired: Name at least one web server in front of the listener, such as 127.0.0.1/32
validation.upstreamBindIp: Enter a loopback or private IPv4 address, such as 127.0.0.1
validation.email: Enter an email address, or leave it empty
validation.certificate: Paste the certificate chain (BEGIN CERTIFICATE) and its private key (PRIVATE KEY), both PEM
validation.sshUser: Use 1 to 64 letters, digits and . _ @ -, not starting with a dot or a hyphen
validation.partnerId: A partner id is exactly 16 hexadecimal digits (0-9, A-F)
validation.partnerPair: Give both partner ids, or neither
validation.panelUrlPath: Only the address of the panel: no path, query or #
validation.panelUrlPort: The port is a number from 1 to 65535
validation.panelUrlHttp: http:// is only for localhost: use https://

errors.unreachable: Cannot reach the panel. Check the connection and try again.
errors.server: The server answered with an error. Try again in a moment.
errors.stale: The panel did not answer. What is shown may be out of date.
errors.notFound: It does not exist, or it has been deleted.
errors.routeTitle: Something went wrong on this page

setup.title: Set up Postern
setup.intro: Create the first administrator. The panel prints the setup token in its log when it starts without an administrator.
setup.tokenHint: From the log of the panel. It is valid for one hour.
setup.done: The administrator was created. Sign in to continue.

login.title: Sign in
login.totpIntro: Enter the 6-digit code from your authenticator app.

overview.title: Overview
overview.empty: No nodes yet. A node is a server that runs the Postern agent: add the first one.

node.edgeBehind: The edge runs {{edge}}, the agent {{agent}}: an edge keeps the binary that it was started with until it is rolled.
node.edgeUnknown: The edge does not say its version: it is older than the agent ({{agent}}), or it does not answer.
node.edgeRoll: Roll it: on the server, run
node.copyRollEdge: Copy the command that rolls the edge

nodes.title: Nodes
nodes.empty: No nodes yet. A node is a server that runs the Postern agent.

detail.noProxies: This node has no proxies yet.
detail.noHost: The node has no address yet: it comes with the first connection, or set it in “Edit the node”.
detail.dangerHint: The node is removed from the panel with its listeners and proxies. The node itself keeps running.

banner.label: What the node needs
banner.provisioning: The node is not connected yet. Install it.
banner.edgeOutdated: The edge runs an old version

egress.intro: How the node reaches Telegram. Its proxies go out through its default chain, unless they have a chain of their own.
egress.defaultChainHint: Without one, the node goes out directly.
egress.dnsModeHint: DNS-over-HTTPS works also on servers where the port of DNS is blocked.
egress.saved: The egress settings of the node were saved.

artifacts.title: Engine binaries
artifacts.intro: Where the node gets the binaries of its engines and providers. Either way the node keeps only a file with the checksum the panel pinned, and tries it out before its first use.
artifacts.sourceDirect: Downloaded by the node from the release
artifacts.directHint: The node downloads over HTTPS itself; the panel uploads what it still lacks at its next check.
artifacts.directUnsupported: The agent of this node is too old to download for itself.
artifacts.saved: Where the node gets its binaries was saved.

mgmt.intro: How the panel reaches the agent of the node: on a port of its own, or hidden behind a public tls listener of the node, by a management SNI that only the panel knows, with the port of its own closed.
mgmt.title: Management of the node
mgmt.sniHint: A host name that is no domain of the proxies of the node. Nobody needs to resolve it.
mgmt.publicPortHint: A tls listener of the node that the panel reaches the agent through.
mgmt.noPorts: The node has no tls listener
mgmt.slow: The panel checks the new path before it keeps it; that can take up to a minute.
mgmt.failed: The mode stays as it was
mgmt.done: The management of the node was switched.

ports.intro: What listens on the TCP ports of the node, as it said the last time that the panel asked it. A listener cannot take a port that another process holds.
ports.none: The node has not said which ports are in use yet.

delete.title: Delete the node?
delete.message: The node {{name}} is deleted from the panel together with its listeners, proxies and statistics. The node itself is not touched: its agent keeps serving the last state that it had.

created.title: The node was created
created.later: These steps are on the page of the node, too.

form.name: Name
form.mgmtHostHint: Where the panel reaches the agent: an IP address or a host name.
form.mgmtPortHintCreate: The port of the agent. Leave empty to pick a random high port.
form.mgmtPortHintEdit: Where the panel connects. The agent keeps listening on the port of the bundle that it was installed from.
form.linkHostHint: The host in the links of the proxies of this node. Leave empty to use the management host.
form.mgmtHostHintCreate: You may leave it empty: the panel takes the address that the node connects from.

install.intro: The node is installed on its server: Linux on x86-64 or arm64, with Docker and the Compose v2 plugin.
install.bundleStep: Download the bundle of the node: its certificate and its private key.
install.secret: The bundle holds the private key of the node: treat it as a secret.
install.kitStep: Download the node kit for the architecture of the server: the postern-node binary with install.sh, launcher.sh and compose.yaml.
install.archHint: uname -m on the server tells it: x86_64 is amd64, aarch64 is arm64.
install.noKit: This panel carries no node kit for {{arch}}. Put a postern-node binary of version {{version}} for {{arch}} on the server as /root/postern/postern-node yourself, and next to it install.sh, launcher.sh and compose.yaml from deploy/node/ of the same release.
install.copyStep: Make the directory on the server and copy both files into it; put the address of the server in place of <SERVER>:
install.copyStepNoKit: Make the directory on the server and copy the bundle into it; put the address of the server in place of <SERVER>:
install.runStep: On the server, in /root/postern, run the install command:
install.manualBlock: Without a registry: kit and bundle

docker.title: Install with one command
docker.intro: The server needs Linux with Docker. Run the command on the server as root: the node joins the panel by itself.
docker.panelUrlHint: Where the node reaches the panel. The browser remembers it.
docker.replaces: Getting a new command cancels the previous one.
docker.composeHint: Save it as compose.yaml on the server and run docker compose up -d.
docker.firewall: The panel connects to the node on the management port {{port}}/tcp: open it in the firewall for the address of the panel. Or turn on hidden management in the Management section.
docker.firewallHidden: The node is in hidden management: the panel comes through its public tls listener, and the management port stays closed.
docker.noImage: The panel has no node image (POSTERN_NODE_IMAGE), so there is no command. The ways below still work.

deploy.openHint: The panel logs in to the server, checks it and installs the node by itself.
deploy.title: Install over SSH
deploy.intro: The panel logs in to the server of {{name}} as root, or as a user with passwordless sudo, checks the server and installs the node there.

target.hostHint: The address of the server for SSH: an IP address or a host name.
target.userHint: root, or a user with passwordless sudo.
target.privateKeyHint: The key in PEM, as ssh-keygen writes it: it starts with -----BEGIN.
target.passphraseHint: Only for a key that has one.
target.savedHint: The panel keeps credentials for {{user}}@{{server}}, sealed.
target.secrets: The panel uses the credentials for this install only, unless you ask it to keep them.
target.panelUrlHint: The node reaches the panel at this address. The same address as on the node page; the browser remembers it.
target.dockerPath: The panel starts the node with one docker run command from the image {{image}}. The server needs only Docker.

hostKey.title: Confirm the host key of the server
hostKey.first: The panel meets this server for the first time. Compare the key that it presents with the key of the server before the panel sends it any credentials.
hostKey.check: On the server, this command prints the fingerprint:
hostKey.changedTitle: The host key of the server has changed
hostKey.changed: The server presents another key than the one that was confirmed for it. The server may have been reinstalled, or someone may be in the middle of the connection. The panel sent it no credentials.
hostKey.trustCheck: I have compared the new key with the one on the server
hostKey.meetAgainHint: The server offers no key of the type that was confirmed. The panel can forget the confirmed key and show you the key that the server has now, to confirm before it sends any credentials.
hostKey.meetAgainCheck: I have checked on the server that its host keys were changed on purpose
hostKey.notSaved: The saved credentials were for the old key, and are not sent to this server: go back and type the credentials.

report.title: What the panel found
report.noKit: {{arch}}, but the panel has no node kit for it
report.portPostern: Held by Postern: the node is installed here already
report.noPublicIps: None on the interfaces (the server may be behind NAT)
report.methodDocker: docker run from the node image
report.blockers: The install is refused for this
report.installDocker: Let the panel set up Docker
report.installDockerHint: An installed Docker is never replaced: the panel starts it, or adds the Compose v2 plugin of its packages. Only where there is no Docker does the panel install it, with the script of get.docker.com, or with the packages of the distribution when that fails.
report.rememberHint: For a later install of this node. Without it the panel forgets them.

issues.not_root: The commands of the panel do not run as root on the server (uid {{uid}}): log in as root, or as a user with passwordless sudo.
issues.arch_unsupported: The server is {{machine}}, and Postern nodes run on amd64 and arm64 only.
issues.kit_missing: The panel has no node kit for {{arch}}: run the panel from its Docker image, which carries the kits.
issues.bash_missing: bash 4 or newer is not installed, and install.sh needs it (on Alpine: apk add bash).
issues.docker_stopped: Docker does not answer: the Docker daemon does not run.
issues.compose_missing: The Docker Compose v2 plugin is missing.
issues.userns_remap: Docker remaps user namespaces (userns-remap), which Postern does not support: remove "userns-remap" from /etc/docker/daemon.json and restart Docker.
issues.mgmt_port_taken: The management port {{port}} of the node is taken by {{owner}}.
issues.ports_unknown: The listening ports of the server could not be read: whether 443 and the management port are free is not known.
issues.clock_ahead: The clock of the server is at least {{seconds}} s ahead of the panel: keep it in sync (NTP).
issues.clock_behind: The clock of the server is at least {{seconds}} s behind the panel: keep it in sync (NTP).
issues.compose_manual: The Docker Compose v2 plugin is missing, and the panel adds none to this Docker ({{origin}}): install Docker Compose v2 by hand.
issues.originUnknown: packages that the panel does not know

job.doneMessage: The node is installed and online.
job.cancelMessage: The panel asks the install on the server to stop: install.sh stops at once, and the program of its current step (apt-get, docker compose) may run to its end. The bundle is removed from the server once install.sh has stopped. The node may be installed in part: install it again later.

proxies.title: Proxies
proxies.empty: No proxies yet. A proxy is one link that you give to its users.
proxies.noNodes: Proxies run on nodes, and there are no nodes yet. Add a node first.

table.outdated: Outdated: it runs another version than it should, or a newer one is on its channel

proxies.copyLinkFailed: Could not copy the link. Open the proxy and copy it from its page.

listeners.title: Listeners
listeners.empty: This node has no listeners yet. A listener is a port that the clients of the proxies connect to.

delete.title: Delete the listener?
delete.message: The listener {{address}} is deleted. A listener that proxies still use cannot be deleted: delete those proxies first.

form.bindIpHint: An IPv4 address of the node; 0.0.0.0 is all of them.
form.bindIpHintUpstream: A loopback or private IPv4 address of the node: the web server in front connects here. 127.0.0.1 is the usual one.
form.portHint: The port that clients connect to.
form.portHintUpstream: The port that the web server in front hands the proxy path to. Ports 20000 to 40999 on 127.0.0.1 are kept for the node itself.
form.linkHostOverrideHint: Used in the links of the proxies on this listener instead of the link host of the node. Leave empty to use the node's.
form.strangerActionHint: What a connection gets whose server name no proxy of this listener has.
form.maskTargetHint: host or host:port, port 443 by default. Leave empty to relay to the server name that the stranger asked for.
form.kindHint: A public port that terminates TLS, or a loopback port behind a web server of the node (for WEB proxies under a path of its site).
form.trustedCidrsHint: The addresses of the web servers in front of the listener, one per line, as prefixes or addresses inside the loopback or private ranges (127.0.0.1/32; the subnet of a Docker bridge). Their X-Forwarded-For is believed: a host inside these ranges chooses its own identity, so name the web servers only.

portTaken.title: Port {{address}} is in use on the node
portTaken.message: {{owners}} listens there. The listener is saved, but the edge cannot listen there until the port is free, and until then the node does not apply its state: its last error says why.

detail.certificateUpstream: Owned by the web server in front

links.qrAlt: QR code of the tg link
links.qrHint: Scan it with the camera of a phone that has Telegram.

live.empty: The node has not reported this proxy since the panel started.
live.caption: The last minute that the node reported

delete.title: Delete the proxy?
delete.message: The proxy {{name}} and its statistics are deleted, and its links stop working. This cannot be undone.

form.warning: The proxy was saved, with a warning
form.noListeners: This node has no listeners yet. Add a listener on the page of the node first.
form.name: Name
form.nameHint: Only for you: it is not in the links.
form.domainHint: The server name that the clients send. Leave empty to get a free domain from the pool of the panel.
form.domainHintEdit: A new domain changes the links. Leave empty to get a free domain from the pool of the panel.
form.secretHint: 32 hexadecimal digits. Leave empty to make a random one. It is shown only inside the links.
form.devicesHint: How many different client IPs may use the proxy at a time.
form.adTagHint: The promotion tag from @MTProxybot: 32 hexadecimal digits. Leave empty for none.
form.egressHint: The chain that the connections of the proxy go out through, and chains of its own for what it does.
form.chainDefault: The default chain of the node
form.scopeMeHint: The connections to the middle proxies of Telegram, which a proxy with an ad tag goes through.
form.scopeFetchHint: What the engine downloads, such as the site that its fake TLS imitates.
form.useMiddleProxyHint: Whether the proxy goes through the middle proxies of Telegram. An ad tag works only through them, and Automatic turns them on when the proxy has one.
form.middleProxyAuto: Automatic: on with an ad tag
form.typeFakeTlsHint: A fake-TLS proxy: the tg://proxy link, a domain that its traffic imitates.
form.typeWebHint: A WEB proxy: the t.me/webproxy link, served over HTTPS on a domain of yours whose A record points at the node.
form.webDomainHint: Your domain, whose A record points at the node (not proxied by Cloudflare). It is the address in the link.
form.webHint: The node terminates TLS for the domain itself and needs a certificate for it.
form.webHintUpstream: The web server in front of the listener owns the domain and its certificate; it hands the base path to the node.
form.basePathHint: A path under the domain, such as tg, or empty for the whole domain.
form.basePathHintUpstream: The path of the site that goes to the proxy, such as tg: segments of letters, digits, _ and -.
form.secretModeHint: How the secret is written in the link: another mode makes another link.
form.carrierHint: https for every client (iOS needs it); https-lanes is offered to clients that negotiate anyway.
form.certModeHint: The node issues one with DNS-01 and renews it, or you paste one that you have.
form.dnsCredentialHint: The Cloudflare token for the zone of the domain, from
form.acmeEmailHint: An email for the certificate authority, or empty.
form.certStored: A certificate is stored ({{sha256}}…). Paste a new pair to replace it, or leave both empty to keep it.
form.certChainHint: fullchain.pem: the certificate of the domain first, then the issuers.
form.certKeyHint: privkey.pem. It is sent to the panel once and kept sealed; it is never shown again.
form.noHost: The node has no address yet: the links of the proxy would have no host.

snippets.title: Web server in front
snippets.intro: Put one of these into the site of the domain on the web server that owns port 443. The whole path goes to the node unchanged, with the real client address; the path without a slash too, so that it does not become a redirect.

versions.title: Engine and version
versions.failed: The node could not bring up {{version}}; the running version kept serving.
versions.pinHint: Pin the proxy to a version, or let it follow the channel of its node.
versions.heldByRollout: A rollout holds this proxy now; the pin can be changed when it is over.
versions.pinRestart: A new version starts next to the running one and takes over by blue-green.
versions.followed: The proxy follows its channel again.

egress.title: Egress
egress.intro: How the nodes reach Telegram. An egress is a way out; a chain puts egresses in the order that the edge tries them, and fails over to the next one that is up.
egress.empty: No egresses yet. A node without a chain goes out directly.
egress.experimentalHint: Psiphon is not confirmed on a real server yet: it may not connect.
egress.refreshed: The nodes that run it fetch the subscription again.
egress.refreshedNone: No node uses the subscription yet.

delete.title: Delete the egress?
delete.message: The egress {{name}} is deleted. An egress that a chain has cannot be deleted: take it out of the chain first.

form.name: Name
form.nodeHint: An egress of a node is for that node only, such as an interface that only it has.
form.interfaceHint: A network interface of the node, such as wg0. Leave empty for the one of the default route.
form.bindIpHint: An address of the node to connect from. Leave empty to let the node pick.
form.passwordKept: A password is stored. Leave empty to keep it while the address and the username stay; type it again for a new address or username; clear the username to remove it.
form.uriHint: vless://, vmess://, trojan:// or ss://. It holds credentials: the panel keeps it sealed and never shows it again.
form.uriKept: Stored: {{masked}}. Leave empty to keep it.
form.urlHint: http or https. The node fetches it every 6 hours. It often holds a token: the panel keeps it sealed and never shows it again.
form.urlKept: Stored: {{masked}}. Leave empty to keep it.
form.selectName: Servers whose name contains a text
form.warpHint: The node registers a WARP device of its own: there is nothing to set.
form.invalid: The panel does not take these settings
form.liveHint: Whether the server answers shows in the egress health of the nodes that use it.
form.partnerHint: Only for an operator with a Psiphon partner agreement. Left empty, the egress uses the ids of a client without one (FFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF).

chain.title: Chains
chain.empty: No chains yet. A chain is made of egresses.

delete.title: Delete the chain?
delete.message: The chain {{name}} is deleted. A chain that a node or a proxy uses cannot be deleted: change those first.

form.name: Name
form.nodeHint: A chain of a node is for that node only, and may have its egresses.
form.membersHint: The edge tries them in this order, and fails over to the next one that is up.
form.checkHint: 0 is the default of the node. A node runs one check for all of its chains: the one of its default chain, or else of the first of its chains that has one.

egressHealth.title: Egress health
egressHealth.intro: How the members of the chains of the node are doing, as the node reported it last: the edge asks a datacenter of Telegram through each of them.
egressHealth.empty: The node has not reported the health of its chains since the panel started.
egressHealth.staleReport: The node has not reported its checks for longer than three of their intervals (at least 2 minutes): these are the last values that it reported.
egressHealth.nodeOffline: The node is not online: these are the last values that it reported, and they may no longer hold.

password.title: Change password
password.hint: All other sessions of this account are signed out.
password.codeHint: The 6-digit code from your authenticator app. A code that was used a moment ago is refused: wait for the next one.

totp.title: Two-factor authentication
totp.intro: Ask for a code from an authenticator app when signing in, in addition to the password.
totp.scan: Scan the QR code with an authenticator app.
totp.qrTitle: QR code with the TOTP secret
totp.manual: Or type the key by hand:
totp.confirmIntro: Then enter the code that the app shows and your password to turn it on.
totp.enabledIntro: A code is asked for at every sign-in. To turn it off, enter your password and a current code.

dns.title: DNS credentials
dns.intro: The tokens that the nodes issue the certificates of WEB proxies with (ACME, DNS-01). A token is stored sealed, handed to the nodes of the proxies that use it, and never shown again.
dns.empty: No credentials yet. A WEB proxy whose certificate the node issues needs one: a Cloudflare API token with Zone:DNS:Edit on the zone of its domain.

form.name: Name
form.nameHint: Only for you: which zone or account the token is for.
form.tokenHint: A Cloudflare API token with Zone:DNS:Edit on the zone of the domain. It is never shown again.
form.tokenHintEdit: Leave empty to keep the stored token. A new one goes to the nodes that use it.

delete.title: Delete the credential?
delete.message: The credential {{name}} is deleted. One that proxies still use cannot be deleted: give them another one first.

versions.title: Versions
versions.intro: The versions of the engines, the egress providers and Postern itself. A channel moves only when a rollout completes: canary first, then the rest, one step at a time.

channel.confirmIntro: This changes the version of these proxies ({{count}}); each one restarts its engine by blue-green:

releases.none: The panel knows no release of this component yet.

rollout.pinVersionHint: Pin the proxies to a version, or let them follow the channel of their node.
rollout.mtgNoteTitle: mtg fronts directly from the node
rollout.mtgNote: mtg's domain fronting dials the mask target directly from the node, not through the egress chain.
rollout.modeManual: Manual: stop after each step until Continue
rollout.modeAuto: Auto: go on by itself after a pause
rollout.moveNote: No proxy follows this channel: it moves to the version at once, with no steps.
rollout.canaryHint: The canary goes first, then the rest of its node, then every other node. A failed step is reverted by itself and stops the rollout.
rollout.skipOfflineHint: A node offline during its step stays on its previous version instead of failing the step.

panel.title: Panel
panel.confirmMessage: The panel installs the signed {{version}} binary and restarts with it. If {{version}} does not start healthy, its launcher goes back to {{current}} and restores the database.
panel.restarting: The panel is restarting with {{version}}. This page reconnects when it is back.
panel.testKeys: The panel was built with test release keys among the keys it trusts. Do not use it in production.
panel.cannotUpdate: The panel cannot update itself now

upload.title: Upload a release bundle
upload.intro: For a panel that cannot reach the release source: a postern-vX.Y.Z-bundle.tar with the signed binaries. It is taken only whole.
upload.refused: The bundle was refused; nothing was kept.
upload.stableRefused: The stable list was not applied: {{reason}}

source.title: Release source
source.tokenSet: A token is set. Type a new one to replace it.
source.removeToken: Remove the token of the source
source.tokensHint: Tokens are write-only: the panel never shows them again. A field left empty keeps the stored token.
source.prereleasesHint: It covers the panel, the nodes and the latest channel of the engines.

reason.web: a WEB proxy: mtg serves fake TLS only
reason.adTag: it has an ad tag, which mtg does not support
reason.middleProxy: the middle proxies are on, which mtg does not have
reason.capability: its node lacks engine-mtg: upgrade the node first

node.title: Versions
node.needsInstall: An update that the node cannot take yet needs a newer node build: re-run install.sh on the node. A node in Docker: run docker rm -f postern-agent and a new install command from the panel (it starts the container from the panel's version), or set the image tag in compose.yaml to the panel's version and run docker compose up -d.

warning.edge-handoff-unsafe: The edge handoff can drop queued connections (tcp_migrate_req is off): re-run install.sh on the node (a node in Docker: docker restart postern-agent).
warning.test-release-keys: The node trusts test release keys.
warning.test-release-keys-ignored: The node was built with test release keys, which it ignores because production keys exist.
